For the Petitioner : Mr. Rohan Mazumdar, Advocate For the State : Mr. Bhola Nath Ojha, A.P.P. For

Order No.05/ Dated:20.04.2023 Heard learned counsel for the parties.

Apprehending his arrest in connection with Complaint Case No. 1780 of 2020 instituted under
Section 498A of the Indian Penal Code and Sections under Section 3/ 4 of the Dowry Prohibition
Act, the petitioner has moved this Court for grant of privilege of anticipatory bail.

As per complaint petition, allegation against the petitioner is that the complainant was married with the petitioner on 27.04.2013 and after marriage, she was subjected to mental and physical torture due to non-fulfilment of the additional dowry was demanded by the petitioner.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is innocent and has committed no offence at all rather he has been falsely implicated in this case.

It is lastly submitted that the petitioner undertake to co- operate with the investigation of the case and also abide by all terms and conditions which may be imposed in the matter of granting anticipatory bail to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner may be extended the privilege of anticipatory bail.
Learned Addl.P.P appearing for the State opposes the prayer for anticipatory bail of the petitioner.
From perusal of record, it appears that complaint case has been lodged due to matrimonial discard.
There is no necessity of custodial trial of the petitioner.

In the light of above facts and circumstances, without expressing any view on the merits of the case,
this anticipatory bail application is disposed off.
